thread:
michael: Heads up — we're seeing a customer-reported p99 spike on chat.generate since 02:10 UTC. Grafana shows p95 ~180ms -> 320ms, p99 from 450ms -> 1.2s. Notified by support ticket #C-9742 :eyes:

sara: link? which model / kernel path?

michael: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/abc/chat-p99?orgId=1&from=now-6h to=now - affected model is rwd-llama-70b-quant, mostly 1k token seqs. Top traces point to attention kernel compile path.

kevin: we had a staggered rollout of a compile-flag yesterday: SDPA_COMPILE_MODE=flashopt -> enabled at 02:05 in canary then global at 02:08 by auto-rollout. Deploy-bot shows the rollout window. :grimacing:

deploy-bot: deploy rwd-runtime@v2.14.3 started 2026-03-15T02:05Z, feature-flag: sdpa-flashopt=true, rollout 02:08 completed in us-west-2 clusters.

eng-oncall: I'm on it, re-running the p99 query now and pulling traces. Priya, can you attach the customer's repro?

priya: customer gave a minimal repro: straight chat.generate with system prompt + 800 token user prompt, sync mode. They see consistent p99 >1s for requests between 02:10-03:00 UTC.

jess: if this lines up with the compile flag, mitigation = pause/refreeze flag and route affected traffic to the fallback kernel path (sdpa-fallback / flash-disabled) while we triage.

kevin: Confirmed. There's a heuristic in kernel-selection that prefers flashopt for >512 seqs now due to cost weight change. Might be mis-ranking for certain shapes causing slower kernels to be chosen.

michael: Traces show kernel switch churn on warm-up: lots of compile churn + 500ms stalls labeled "nvrtc compile wait" in the timeline. Stack: `runtime/attn/compile.cpp:274` -> `kernel_launcher` -> nvrtc.

lina: Good call. Let's cut the rollout flag globally: `curl -XPOST https://flags.redwood/api/toggle -d '{"flag":"sdpa-flashopt","value":false}'` then restart pool-grpc workers with rc rolling restart. I'll prep commands. :rocket:

kevin: Also pushing a quick hotpatch to kernel-selection heuristics: reduce flashopt preference weight for shapes from 513-1024 and set a hysteresis window to avoid flips for 5m. I'll open a PR but want to hold rollout first.

jess: Agreed. Priya — tell the customer we are rolling back the compile flag and will follow up with RCA. Keep them in standby for a short window verification. :thumbsup:

priya: On it. Messaging now.

eng-oncall: Repro steps I ran: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat.generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-70b-quant","input":"<system>...<800 token user>"}'
```
Observed timeline snippet:
```
[02:12:33] kernel select: sdpa-flashopt (compiled)
[02:12:33] nvrtc compile start
[02:12:34] nvrtc compile end
[02:12:34] token emit delay 540ms
```

michael: If rollback helps we should also capture the compile artifacts and logs to reproduce locally. Kevin — can you dump the nvrtc args and kernel config for that run?

kevin: grabbing `dl/compile_cache/2026-03-15/usw2/*` now. Two suspicious flags: `-O3 -fno-fast-math` and kernel param `grid_y=1` fallback. I'll attach.

lina: Rollback started. Commands: 
```
# flip flag
POST /flags/sdpa-flashopt false
# restart worker RCs
kubectl rollout restart deployment/worker-pool -n runtime --selector=pool=usw2
```
Rollback completed across 3 clusters at 02:28 UTC.

deploy-bot: feature flag sdpa-flashopt set to false by lina at 2026-03-15T02:28Z. Worker restarts completed (3/3).

eng-oncall: Recomputed p99 after rollback (02:35-02:45): p95 ~190ms, p99 ~480ms. Looks back to baseline. Customer confirm?

priya: Customer reports improved latency within 5m of rollback. They confirmed: p99 now ~450ms. Sending follow-up note. :pray:

jess: Next steps: 1) revert the global compile flag (done) 2) collect compile artifacts and perf traces 3) create a controlled canary with additional telemetry (nvrtc durations, kernel runtime) 4) update kernel-selection heuristic PR and add a test for 513-1024 shape class.

kevin: I'll open PR #5124 with heuristic changes + perf test. Also propose warming compile cache offline (precompile common shapes) to avoid nvrtc in hot path.

michael: Filing incident doc and tagging for postmortem re: too-aggressive rollout heuristics. Lina/Jess assign owners for RCA.

lina: I'll own rollback/runbook update. Jess will own heuristic change. Kevin will own compile-cache prewarm.

priya: Customer SLO credits requested — submitting billing note.

eng-oncall: marking this thread resolved for oncall after postmortem starts. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
